关键词: Texas A&M University's Mays Business School
主要内容: The Great Resignation has fundamentally changed the workplace, according to Anthony Klotz, the expert who coined the term. Klotz, a management professor at Texas A&M University's Mays Business School, predicted in May 2021 that the pandemic would lead to a surge in resignations. Since then, millions of Americans have quit their jobs, with a record 4.5 million workers leaving in March alone. The initial wave of resignations was due to a backlog of departures that had been delayed during the height of the pandemic. Many employees were also burned out, unhappy, and reevaluating their lives. Employers have adapted to meet these needs, offering remote work opportunities and focusing on employee wellness, including mental and financial health. Klotz emphasized that the pandemic brought the future of work into the present, and that the changes are here to stay. He noted that flexibility and autonomy in work arrangements are now key priorities for job seekers, with 63% of job seekers citing work-life balance as a top priority. The Great Resignation has also led to a surge in new business formation, with applications hitting 5.4 million last year.
